rationale: Extensive literature confirms that FDXR-associated disease (MMDS9B / ANOA, OMIM #617717 / #620887) differs fundamentally in its primary clinical presentation from MMDS1-3. While MMDS1-3 characteristically present with catastrophic neonatal lactic acidosis, fatal pulmonary hypertension, and cystic leukodystrophy due to deficient lipoic acid synthase and severe glycine cleavage/pyruvate dehydrogenase defects, FDXR variants typically present with childhood- or juvenile-onset progressive sensorial neuropathy (predominantly auditory neuropathy spectrum disorder and optic atrophy), sensory-motor polyneuropathy, or ataxia. Counter-examples demonstrating severe early mortality (such as infant death following infection reported by Yang et al., 2021) remain exceptions characterized as unusually severe rather than typical presentations. The predominant phenotype remains post-synaptic auditory neuropathy, optic atrophy, and subacute post-infectious neuromuscular weakness/ataxia mimicking Guillain-Barré syndrome.

evidence.text: Biallelic mutations in FDXR cause sensorial neuropathies manifesting as auditory neuropathy spectrum disorder and optic atrophy in eight patients across four families without early neonatal metabolic collapse or cystic leukodystrophy.

source.title: FDXR mutations cause sensorial neuropathies and expand the spectrum of mitochondrial Fe-S-synthesis diseases
source.quote: Here, we report on eight subjects from four independent families affected by auditory neuropathy and optic atrophy. Whole-exome sequencing revealed biallelic mutations in FDXR in affected subjects of each family.

evidence.text: A comprehensive review of 46 individuals with biallelic FDXR variants established auditory neuropathy and optic atrophy as the defining hallmarks, accompanied by ataxia and peripheral neuropathy.

source.title: Biallelic FDXR mutations induce ferroptosis in a rare mitochondrial disease with ataxia
source.quote: The most prevalent clinical features included auditory neuropathy and optic atrophy, followed by ataxia, peripheral neuropathy, and intellectual disability.

evidence.text: Evaluation of syndromic non-isolated auditory neuropathy identified FDXR variants as presenting with hearing loss (onset 2 to 25 years, mean 11 years) accompanied by motor weakness, ataxia, and pes cavus rather than catastrophic early metabolic decompensation.

source.title: Identification of genetic mechanisms of non-isolated auditory neuropathy with various phenotypes in Chinese families
source.quote: Patients' age of hearing loss onset ranged from 2 to 25 years, averaging 11 years. Hearing loss varied from mild to profound, with 57.1%(4/7) of patients having risk factors and 71.4%(5/7) exhibiting additional systemic symptoms such as muscle weakness, ataxia, and high arches.

evidence.text: Five patients with biallelic FDXR variants exhibited early optic atrophy, acoustic neuropathy, developmental delay, and progressive retinal dystrophy with vascular attenuation, confirming predominant neuro-ophthalmic and auditory pathology.

source.title: FDXR-associated disease in a Chinese cohort
source.quote: FDXR: associated disease is characterized by optic atrophy, acoustic neuropathy, and developmental delays. This study evaluated the ocular phenotypes and genetic features of patients with biallelic FDXR variants. Five individuals from unrelated non-consanguineous Chinese families with biallelic FDXR variants were identified

evidence.text: A severe outlier case of FDXR deficiency presented with hearing loss, visual impairment, and motor retardation that culminated in infantile death following infection, showing that while rare, severe post-infectious infantile mortality can occur.

source.title: Report of a case with ferredoxin reductase (FDXR) gene variants in a Chinese boy exhibiting hearing loss, visual impairment, and motor retardation
source.quote: Compared with the reported cases, except hearing loss and visual impairment, the clinical manifestations of this boy were more serious, who also had motor retardation and died in infancy after infection.

new_directions.question_text: What specific biochemical and iron-homeostasis parameters distinguish FDXR deficiency from late-stage ISC assembly defects (NFU1, BOLA3, IBA57) in clinical screening?
new_directions.rationale: Determining whether lipoic-acid-dependent enzyme activities (pyruvate dehydrogenase, alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase) and serum glycine are strictly normal in FDXR patients will provide rapid diagnostic laboratory separation from classical MMDS1-3 prior to whole-exome sequencing.

new_directions.question_text: What proportion of patients misdiagnosed with Guillain-Barré syndrome harboring refractory, relapsing post-infectious quadriparesis harbor pathogenic FDXR variants?
new_directions.rationale: Screening cohorts of pediatric and juvenile atypical or IVIG-unresponsive GBS cases for FDXR variants can assess how frequently this metabolic-sensorial neuropathy mimics autoimmune demyelinating polyneuropathy.
